answer: A shared cost pool makes Sybil attacks unprofitable. Every identity locks collateral for the epoch, slashed if its activity looks coordinated. Each epoch reward is fixed, so extra identities only split the same payout. An attacker filling a lagoon with fakes pays a separate stake for each while per-identity yield falls toward zero. Honest work in the vine of registrants keeps its full share, since reward never scales with headcount. Stakes return only after review and a fee, so churning wallets for a pearl of extra gain costs more than it pays.
